background_notes.fact: For a smooth Sobolev-valued path G on [a,c], K(t)=integral_a^t G(s)ds is differentiable with K'=G, K(a)=0 and ||K(t)||<=integral_a^t||G(s)||ds. These facts apply to the integrands defining F, Cst, Q and rho on the current smooth step.

grounds.reason: Interp is formed from time integrals of B applied to smooth step data and their stages.
B is defined by smooth Fourier evolution, multiplication and a spatial derivative on smooth inputs.
Rem on smooth inputs is defined by absolutely convergent rapidly decreasing Fourier series and is fixed on each step.

background_notes.justification: For continuous Banach-space-valued G, the difference between a difference quotient of its integral and G(t) is bounded by the supremum of ||G(s)-G(t)|| on the shrinking interval; hence it tends to zero. The integral norm inequality follows from triangle inequalities for Riemann sums and their limits. Smooth spatial data remain smooth under the Fourier multipliers here: any fixed number of space/time derivatives introduces only polynomial frequency factors, absorbed by rapid Fourier decay. Finite products and these time integrals preserve smoothness.

background_notes.fact: For J=[a,t] contained in K=[a,a+tau], X(K) bounds restrict to X(J) with no larger norm. A constant-in-time L2 function f has weak derivative zero and ||f||_(X(J))<=||f||_2. Also ||f||_2<=||f||_(H^gamma) when gamma>=0.

grounds.reason: X is the sum of the L-infinity L2 norm and the L-infinity H^(-pstar) derivative norm.
The needed Y and z norms are supplied on the full step; f is a fixed L2 step datum.

background_notes.justification: Restriction cannot increase essential suprema and preserves the weak derivative. A constant path has zero distributional derivative. Each Fourier weight is at least one for gamma>=0, so comparison of the nonnegative sums gives the Sobolev-to-L2 inequality. These facts justify N006 on initial subintervals and the norm comparisons later in S005.

background_notes.fact: A continuous path obtained by concatenating finitely many smooth pieces has distributional derivative equal to its piecewise derivative, with no point masses at joins. If each piecewise derivative is bounded in H^(-pstar) by K, the weak derivative belongs to L-infinity H^(-pstar) with norm at most K.

grounds.reason: N007 supplies a finite continuous piecewise smooth numerical interpolation with matching grid values.
Each residual increment starts at zero and has its H^(-pstar) derivative bounded.
Rres is constructed by adding each new step increment to the preceding endpoint; v is smooth.
X uses weak derivatives and essential suprema.

background_notes.justification: Integrate each smooth piece against a compactly supported scalar test-function derivative. Integration by parts gives endpoint terms that cancel pairwise by continuity. The remaining integral is the pairing with the piecewise derivative. Finite joins have measure zero, so its essential supremum is at most the maximum piecewise bound. This applies to V, Rres and e=v-V.
